correctness.rationale: The optimal lower bound A is the supremum of lambda with lambda KK* <= S_Lambda, so the least coefficient mu with KK* <= mu S_Lambda is exactly 1/A. Every K-dual factorization K=T_Lambda T_Gamma* gives KK* <= ||T_Gamma||^2 S_Lambda, proving the corrected lower bound. The one-dimensional example Lambda_1=2I gives A=4 and dual norm squared 1/4. The two-dimensional frame (e1,e1,2e2) has A=2 and an explicit interval of distinct duals whose dual frame operator is diag(1/2,1/4+2t^2), so all |t|<=1/(2sqrt(2)) attain the sharp value 1/2. These exact calculations independently verify both defects.

value.rationale: Theorem 2.4 is the paper's defining canonical K-dual norm characterization and its normalization was copied into later K-g-frame generalizations. The error changes the sharp constant by a reciprocal and can reverse inequalities by arbitrarily large factors under simple rescaling. The second defect changes the claimed uniqueness structure: a three-vector frame has a continuum of sharp minimizers. The repair precisely separates the sharp norm value from the extra Douglas reduced-range condition that singles out the canonical solution.
